plan: Store a deep copy of the input dict as the single internal tree; to_data() returns a fresh deep copy so callers can never alias internal state.
Provide one pre-order recursive generator over items; total_word_count() and unresolved_markers() both consume it, keeping traversal logic in one place.
For notes, strip [[?identifier]] markers (regex, replaced with a space) before counting words with \b\w+\b; references contribute their declared word_count and their unresolved list verbatim.
Collect marker identifiers into a set (note markers plus reference unresolved lists) and return them sorted lexicographically.
Render the outline recursively with a depth parameter: workspace title at depth 0, each item as two-spaces-per-level + '<kind>: <title>', recursing into section/group items.

Implement move as validate-then-mutate: check id types, locate the item and its parent list, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group id), reject non-containers and missing ids, reject destinations inside the moved item's subtree via a subtree-id set, and bounds-check the index — all before the single pop/insert, so any failure leaves the tree untouched.
mechanisms: Deep-copied internal tree with deep-copy export (constructor and to_data)
Shared pre-order traversal generator over nested items
Regex marker stripping prior to \b\w+\b word tokenization for notes
Set-union then lexicographic sort for unresolved marker identifiers
Depth-parameterized recursive outline renderer with two-space indentation per level
Validate-then-mutate move: parent lookup, destination resolution, subtree-id cycle rejection, insertion-index bounds check, then a single pop/insert
